findings.title: pageCount undercounts pages when totalItems is not divisible by pageSize
findings.whyItBreaks: Math.floor truncates instead of rounding up: pageCount(10, 3) returns 3 instead of 4. Any totalItems with a non-zero remainder against pageSize yields page count = exactPages, so the trailing partial page is never generated — callers iterating pages 1..pageCount silently omit the last (totalItems % pageSize) items (e.g. items 10-12 of 12 with pageSize 3 are unreachable). This is a wrong-count regression on an exported pagination primitive; every consumer that sizes or iterates pages inherits it.

findings.title: Restore Math.ceil so pageCount covers the final partial page
findings.whyItBreaks: pageCount(totalItems, pageSize) must return the number of pages needed to hold totalItems; any totalItems % pageSize != 0 case now returns one page short (e.g. pageCount(10, 3) = 3 instead of 4, pageCount(5, 10) = 0 instead of 1). Callers that iterate 1..pageCount or render pagination UI will silently omit the trailing items or show zero pages for a non-empty list — a data-truncation class regression, and the exported function's name/doc contract ('count of pages') promises the ceiling, not the floor.

findings.title: Fix pageCount to round up; floor drops items on the last page
findings.whyItBreaks: pageCount's contract (its name and prior behavior) is the number of pages needed to hold totalItems; that requires ceiling. With totalItems=10, pageSize=3, base returns Math.ceil(10/3)=4 pages covering all 10 items; head returns Math.floor(10/3)=3, so items 9-10 fall off the last page. Any caller iterating pages 1..pageCount will silently omit trailing records (e.g., a paginator loop that stops at page 3). The error only appears when totalItems % pageSize != 0, so it looks fine on exact-multiple inputs and is easy to miss.

findings.title: Payment gate on canProceed blocks legitimate draft saves in saveDraft
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed is shared by submitOrder (@src/actions.ts:4) and saveDraft (@src/actions.ts:9). Adding `order.payment === "paid"` makes canProceed({state:"draft", payment:"missing"}) return false, so saveDraft — which previously returned "saved" on the base — now returns "blocked" for any unpaid order. Saving a draft is legitimately executable independently of payment (drafts exist precisely for unpaid orders), so this is a regression on a live path, not intended tightening.

findings.title: Shared canProceed payment check now blocks saving unpaid drafts
findings.whyItBreaks: canProceed is one predicate gating two distinct actions. Payment status is a legitimate precondition for submitOrder, but not for saveDraft. After this change, order={state:"draft", payment:"missing"} flips canProceed from true to false, so saveDraft(order) returns "blocked" instead of "saved" at src/actions.ts:9-10 — a user can no longer save an unpaid draft, an action that was legitimately allowed before and has nothing to do with payment state.

findings.title: Split payment check out of canProceed so saveDraft is not blocked
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed predicate `order.state !== "ready" && order.payment === "paid"` gates two distinct actions. For order = {state: "draft", payment: "missing"}, canProceed returned true before (state !== "ready") and false after (payment !== "paid"). submitOrder blocking an unpaid order is plausibly intended, but saveDraft @ src/actions.ts:9 shares the same predicate: saving an unpaid draft is legitimately approvable on its own, and it now returns "blocked" for every unpaid draft — a user-facing regression that can discard unsaved draft input. Payment state has no legitimate bearing on saving a draft.

findings.title: Restore CI workflow: moving .github/workflows/ci.yml to docs/ci.md disables CI
findings.whyItBreaks: The diff renames the repo's only workflow file (.github/workflows/ci.yml -> docs/ci.md, similarity 100%). GitHub Actions only executes workflow files under .github/workflows/, and `git ls-tree -r <head>` confirms the head tree contains no .github/workflows/ directory at all. After merge, `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` (docs/ci.md lines 9-11) silently stop running on every push and pull_request — no red X, just absent checks — while README.md line 5 still promises 'CI runs lint and tests on every push'. All future changes merge unverified.

findings.title: Removing .github/workflows/ci.yml silently disables all CI checks
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub executes workflows only from .github/workflows/. Renaming ci.yml to docs/ci.md (similarity 100% rename in this diff) removes the repo's only workflow: after this PR, `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` no longer run on any push or pull request. `git ls-tree e5865a2` confirms head contains only .needlefish/answers.json, README.md, docs/ci.md, and src/index.ts — no workflow remains anywhere. Unverified, un-linted code can now merge, and README.md:5 ('CI runs lint and tests on every push.') is now false, actively misleading contributors and reviewers who rely on check status.

findings.title: Restore CI workflow — moving ci.yml out of .github/workflows disables CI
findings.whyItBreaks: GitHub Actions only discovers workflow files under .github/workflows/. The rename moved the sole workflow (name: ci, on: push/pull_request, running npm ci / npm run lint / npm test) to docs/ci.md; at head there is no .github directory at all, so pushes and PRs no longer run lint or tests. README.md:5 still promises 'CI runs lint and tests on every push', so the repo's quality gate is silently gone while the docs claim it exists — unlinted, untested code can merge.

findings.title: Remove dbg!(items); — it moves items and breaks the build
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!` expands to `match $val { tmp => { eprintln!(...); tmp } }`, so `dbg!(items)` moves the non-Copy `Vec<String>` out of `items` and the value-statement form `dbg!(items);` drops it immediately. Line 3 (`items.len()`) then triggers E0382 'use of moved value', so the whole crate fails to compile — every downstream consumer of `process` is blocked, and `total` would be unreachable even if it compiled.

findings.title: dbg!(items) moves items, breaking compilation of process()
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!` expands to `match { ... }` taking its argument by value and returning it. `items: Vec<String>` is not `Copy`, so line 2 `dbg!(items);` moves `items` into the macro and drops it. Line 3 `items.len()` then uses the moved value, producing E0382 ('use of moved value: `items`'). The entire crate fails to compile — `cargo build`, tests, and any dependent code are unusable. Additionally, even if fixed to borrow, `dbg!` is a leftover debug macro printing the full item list to stderr in release builds.

findings.title: Remove leftover dbg! debug print from store::process
findings.whyItBreaks: `dbg!(items)` unconditionally formats and prints the entire `Vec<String>` to stderr on every call to the public `process()`. `dbg!` is not stripped in release builds, so shipped code emits uncontrolled debug output and can leak whatever data the store items contain to stderr; a strict reviewer would block this pre-merge.

findings.title: Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY to avoid blocking writes during migration
findings.whyItBreaks: SERIAL syntax identifies PostgreSQL. A non-CONCURRENTLY CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on `users` for the full index build, blocking all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (and on large tables potentially reads) for the migration's duration. Any production-shaped deployment of this migration stalls the app until the index build finishes, and a rollback/abort on timeout leaves no applied migration.

findings.title: Restore commit_id pinning in postReview fallback API call
findings.whyItBreaks: The deleted `-f commit_id=${headSha}` arguments were the only mechanism pinning the fallback review to the reviewed commit. GitHub's create-review API defaults commit_id to the branch's latest commit, so when the primary --input call throws and this fallback runs, the review verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED/APPROVE from VERDICT_EVENT) is submitted against the current PR head rather than headSha. If the PR head moved between review start (src/adapters/github.ts:141) and the fallback submit, a verdict computed on the old commit is applied to an unreviewed newer commit — the exact failure the primary path's `commit_id: headSha` (src/adapters/github.ts:89) exists to prevent. The fallback is inconsistent with the primary path, defeating the code's evident intent.

findings.title: Fallback review post no longer pins commit_id to the reviewed head SHA
findings.whyItBreaks: postReview's catch-path fallback (used when the --input JSON call fails) now posts the review without commit_id. The GitHub reviews API then defaults commit_id to the PR's current head commit. If the PR head moved between review generation (headSha captured earlier) and this fallback post, the review body — describing findings for the old head — is anchored to a newer commit, so findings reference code that is no longer the head, and review state can be anchored to a commit that was never reviewed. The primary path (line 89) intentionally pins commit_id=headSha; the fallback silently lost that guarantee.

findings.title: Stop silently dropping bundle.focus in the large-PR deep review path
findings.whyItBreaks: reviewSmall serializes the whole bundle (incl. focus/deep) to review.md, but reviewLarge no longer substitutes {{FOCUS}} into deep.md. deep.md is built by loadPrompt("deep.md") and the base revision substituted {{FOCUS}} from it, proving the template contains that token; the head revision leaves the literal '{{FOCUS}}' unresolved in every deep-review prompt and the caller-supplied focus directive is silently ignored for large PRs. A user who passes `focus` gets their requested review area applied on small diffs and silently discarded on large ones — the review agent then reports PASS while the focus area was never directed to be reviewed.

findings.title: Stop silently dropping focus/deep on large-PR path; template placeholder left unsubstituted
findings.whyItBreaks: The diff removes `.replace("{{FOCUS}}", bundle.focus ?? "(none)")` from the deep-prompt assembly (base review.ts:120) without changing the prompt template (patchStat shows review.ts is the only changed file). String.replace on a missing target is a no-op, so `prompts/deep.md`'s `{{FOCUS}}` placeholder is now shipped to the model verbatim on every deep pass. Additionally, focus and deep are removed from mapBundle (review.ts:83-89), so the map pass no longer sees them either, while reviewSmall (review.ts:52-55) still JSON-serializes the full bundle including focus and deep. Net effect: a user-supplied focus string is honored on small PRs but silently ignored on large PRs — no error, no signal, wrong review scope on exactly the PRs where scoping matters most (TRIGGER C-style contract drift: the Bundle.focus carrier still promises the behavior, the changed body no longer implements it).
